CONFIRM C0038

CHALLENGE C0011 | The proposed fix adds a standard library dependency (`import statistics`) to compute a median for a very small array (e.g., 5 model timings). The existing `sorted(values)[len // 2]` is functionally sufficient for a PoC pacing signal. Adding this complexity violates the PoC standard to "Ignore LOW entirely" and use the "simplest sufficient fix".

CHALLENGE C0031 | The proposed fix is dead code. The `tools_available` dictionary is initialized as a fresh empty dict `{}` inside `scan_health()` every time it is called. Checking it before running a tool will never skip anything because it holds no state from prior runs.

CHALLENGE C0042 | Language models reliably output the ASCII `->` sequence when specifying line replacements. Demanding the Unicode `→` character will silently break the regex parser for nearly all model-generated proposed fixes, actively degrading system functionality.

MERGE C0043 <- C0030

DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` executes `test_cmd` against the post-fix sandbox code but never runs the test command on the pre-fix source to establish a baseline. If the project's test suite natively has existing test failures (e.g., tests failing on `main` for an unrelated bug), `test_result.returncode` will be non-zero, causing `tests_passed` to be `False`. `_compute_fix_verdict()` will then unconditionally evaluate the fix as `HARMFUL`, meaning no fixes can ever be accepted while the test suite is broken.
FOLLOW: Without a pre-fix test baseline, preexisting test failures will permanently blockade all fix verification and immune pipeline bug closures.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — execute `test_cmd` on the original source code (or unpatched sandbox) first to get a baseline `pre_test_returncode`. Update the verdict logic to only mark the fix `HARMFUL` if tests passed pre-fix but failed post-fix (e.g., `tests_passed = (post_test_result.returncode <= pre_test_returncode)`).
